title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for Downstream Payers
one_liner: Recover itemized tariff surcharges from suppliers who were refunded the tariffs, on contingency, and give surcharge-collecting firms a defensive ledger.
customer: Small contractors, restaurants, repair shops and retailers who were invoiced a separate 'tariff surcharge' line by suppliers in 2025-26, plus small firms that added such surcharges to their own customers' bills.
problem: SCOTUS ruled on 2026-02-20 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, and about $166B in CBP refunds go to the importer of record (about $81B paid by July). Over 40% of small firms saw tariff cost increases and 76% of international sourcers passed them on, so the firm that paid the pass-through gets nothing. Each claim is too small ($200-$8k) for a lawyer, and firms that billed surcharges to their own customers now carry their own exposure.
solution: Read-only scan of the owner's mailbox and QuickBooks/Xero pulls every tariff or surcharge line from vendor invoices and from the firm's own customer invoices. It builds a two-sided surcharge ledger (paid upstream, collected downstream), then generates supplier demand letters that cite the invoice wording and contract terms. Unpaid claims escalate to small-claims templates or a partner attorney. Claims are strongest where the invoice said the surcharge was itemized or refundable. Because one supplier can owe hundreds of customers, settlements can be negotiated per supplier instead of per claim.
why_now: Refunds have been flowing through CBP's automated system since April 2026, so suppliers are holding refund cash right now, before it is absorbed into margins. Invoice records are fresh and 2026 books have not closed.
revenue_model: 25-30% contingency on recovered dollars, with a $49 flat fee for the ledger and audit. Later, a per-supplier settlement-program fee.
non_obvious_insight: Refund law is written for importers, but the money trail is an invoice trail. Itemized invoices are contract evidence, and thousands of tiny claims against a few hundred suppliers form a portfolio no law firm will touch. The same ledger doubles as a defense file for firms that billed surcharges.
first_30_days: Offer a free 'surcharge audit' in trade-specific Facebook groups and subreddits (HVAC, restaurant equipment, apparel resellers). Hand-review 50 mailboxes and find the 10 suppliers with the most itemized surcharges. Retain a consumer-protection attorney to review the demand-letter template, send the first 100 letters, and measure the response rate.

title: Beneficiary-Funded Dynamic Line Ratings
one_liner: Skip the utility's missing incentive: let the data center or generator that needs capacity pay for dynamic line ratings and take a slice of the capacity released.
customer: Data center developers and congestion-constrained renewable, storage and merchant generation owners. The utility is a passive partner.
problem: Dynamic line rating adds 30-50% capacity at about a tenth of the cost of reconductoring, but utilities earn no return on operating savings, so adoption is stuck. Projects held back by a few constrained lines lose years or revenue.
solution: A special-purpose company funds and deploys DLR (sensors plus weather-model virtual ratings) on the specific lines limiting a beneficiary's project. A three-party agreement has the utility accept ratings with a safety margin and keep the reliability data, the beneficiary gets earlier energization or less curtailment, and the company earns a capacity-uplift fee for about 10 years.
why_now: Automated study tools (Tapestry ran ~220 GW of PJM applications in under an hour) show speed is possible. FERC's ambient-adjusted ratings rule and GETs consideration laws mainstream the concept. Cost of delay is enormous.
revenue_model: Cost-plus up-front sensors and analytics, plus an annual $/kW capacity-uplift fee or a share of avoided curtailment.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders wait for the utility's incentive to change, and it will not. Contract the incentive from the customer instead. That is structurally a customer-funded upgrade, which utilities already know how to accept.
first_30_days: Use public congestion and rating data to find the 20 lines most limiting renewables and large loads. Sell three $25-60k congestion and rating audits to constrained project owners. Recruit one utility engineering champion. Resell sensors from an existing DLR vendor.

title: Micropollutant Bill Calculator for Generic Drug Makers
one_liner: A dataset and model that estimates each pharma and cosmetics company's share of Europe's new micropollutant treatment bill, sold first to generic manufacturers who cannot pass the cost on.
customer: Generic and OTC drug manufacturers and their trade body, cosmetics makers, and the national producer-responsibility bodies being created to run the scheme. Companies pay subscriptions, and the bodies pay for the allocation licence.
problem: Step one: the revised Urban Wastewater Directive makes pharma and cosmetics makers pay at least 80% of quaternary treatment, with the payment scheme due by end-2028. Cost estimates differ by roughly 10x (EC 1.2B euros, JRC 1.56B, EurEau 3.6-11.2B, Spain alone 24.5B). Step two: each state must allocate cost by load. Step three: generics makers work on thin margins under tender pricing and cannot pass costs through, so they will drop low-margin molecules, causing shortages. Nobody owns the allocation dataset.
solution: A compound-level model of the top 100 active ingredients and cosmetic ingredients: sales volumes from national statistics, excretion and removal rates, ecotoxicity thresholds and plant-upgrade timelines (20% of large plants by 2033, 60% by 2039, 100% by 2045). Output: estimated cost share per marketing-authorisation holder, by state and year, with scenario bands. Compare allocation keys (by mass versus toxicity-weighted).
why_now: Member states are drafting schemes in 2026-2028, and industry lobbying starts now. The 10x cost disagreement means the first credible number will anchor the negotiation.
revenue_model: $30-120k/yr subscriptions per company, $10-20k workshops, and licences to scheme administrators.
non_obvious_insight: The fight is not over whether pharma pays but over how the allocation key is defined, and generics makers and originators want opposite keys. Owning the neutral dataset means owning the terms of the negotiation.
first_30_days: Publish a free 'top 30 molecules' liability preview using public consumption and removal data. Email regulatory-affairs heads at 20 generics makers in Spain, Italy, Poland and India, and at the generics trade body. Sell the first paid workshop for 10-20k euros.

title: The Second Ceremony After Direct Cremation
one_liner: A scattering-day and celebration-of-life concierge for the majority of families who chose cremation with no service and later realize they need a ritual.
customer: Adult children aged 40 to 65, two to twelve months after a direct cremation of a parent. Channels: online direct-cremation providers, hospice social workers and estate attorneys.
problem: The NFDA projects a 63.4% US cremation rate for 2025, rising toward 82% by 2045, and direct cremation ($1,000 to $3,000, no viewing, no service) is the fastest-growing segment. Families later improvise: an urn in a closet, a scattering with unclear legality, a restaurant back room. Funeral homes make nothing on this, and direct-cremation providers do not offer events.
solution: Fixed-price packages. Scattering day: jurisdiction-specific permit and rule guidance, boat or site scouting, a celebrant, a biodegradable urn, photographer or drone, and a livestream for distant relatives. Celebration of life: venue, catering, an AI-assisted slideshow built from the family's photos, an officiant, a guestbook and thank-you notes. Keepsake add-ons such as glass, vinyl, reef or tree. A planner keyed to 'days since death' nudges families at 30, 60 and 90 days.
why_now: Direct cremation took off with online price comparison, and the NFDA's 2025 report finds most people (58.3%) have attended a funeral at a non-traditional location. AI makes the slideshow, program and eulogy drafting cheap. Cremation providers are looking for post-sale revenue and a 'what now' answer for customers.
revenue_model: $900 to $4,500 per event: a $500 to $1,200 coordination fee plus 15% to 25% margin on boats, venues and catering. A 10% to 15% referral share to cremation providers that embed the offer. Annual remembrance add-on.
non_obvious_insight: Direct cremation removed the ceremony from the funeral bundle, and the vacuum reappears months later when the buyer is calmer, has a longer planning horizon and pays for meaning rather than logistics. The unbundled piece is the second funeral, and it can be more profitable than the first because there is no legacy funeral-home cost base.
first_30_days: Choose a coastal city such as San Diego, Seattle or Boston. Contract two licensed boat charters, three celebrants and a photographer. Write one-page scattering compliance sheets for the local jurisdictions. Interview hospice social workers to find referrals, and offer 10 founding families a $650 scattering-day package. Ask two direct-cremation providers to link the offer from their post-cremation emails, and aim for five events by month three.

title: Step-Down Club: Maintenance After the Max Dose
one_liner: A cheap maintenance membership that turns the majority of GLP-1 users who quit or plateau into a planned step-down and a monetizable restart.
customer: Adults 3-12 months into a cash-pay GLP-1 who have hit goal or are about to quit over cost (consumer pays); telehealths and pharmacies pay a bounty per verified restart.
problem: About one-third of non-diabetic obesity patients are still on therapy at 1 year. Stoppers regain roughly 4x faster than people who lost weight with behavior change, and ~60% of ex-users say they intend to restart. Every company optimizes for staying on the max dose, and nobody sells the middle path or owns the ex-user.
solution: At plateau, a physician-written protocol steps the user down to the lowest effective dose or a planned holiday. A connected scale plus waist and strength check-ins run on SMS. Pre-agreed regain triggers (e.g. +3% above nadir for 2 consecutive weeks) auto-route the user to the cheapest legitimate restart, such as a $149 pill program. Optional 'regain warranty' credit as an add-on.
why_now: SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN (Lancet, 2026) is the first RCT showing a reduced 5 mg tirzepatide dose kept about 70% of the weight loss (-16.6% vs -21.9% at max dose vs -9.9% on placebo). $149-$299 pills (Wegovy pill Jan 2026, Foundayo Apr 2026) make restart cheap. Telehealths are converging on the same price and now compete on acquisition cost.
revenue_model: $19-29/month membership, plus $75-150 partner bounty per verified restart or step-down conversion (a telehealth's first-fill CAC is est. $150-400), plus optional warranty add-on.
non_obvious_insight: Discontinuation is the modal outcome, not a failure mode. A restart is a lead worth more than the membership fee, so whoever owns the ex-user relationship owns the cheapest reacquisition channel in a market where every competitor sells the same drug at the same price.
first_30_days: Recruit 100 plateaued or ex-users from r/Zepbound, r/Semaglutide and Facebook groups. Have an obesity-medicine MD write the step-down and restart protocol. Run the check-ins on SMS with a BYO or $25 scale. Sign one telehealth or pharmacy partner for a per-restart bounty. Charge $19/month from day one.

title: Depot Finder for Robotaxi Fleets
one_liner: A power-first site database and brokerage matching robotaxi fleets to half-empty garages, office podiums and big-box lots with unused electric service.
customer: Robotaxi fleet operators and their depot partners (AV company real-estate teams and fleet contractors such as Moove, Avis and Lyft's Flexdrive) in launch cities, and owners of distressed garages and office podiums.
problem: AV fleets need charging and cleaning depots near service zones with megawatts of power and workable zoning, while utility interconnection takes 18-36 months. Meanwhile downtown garages and office podiums have oversized electrical service and falling parking revenue.
solution: A ranked site database using proximity to service zones, available service capacity (utility maps and permits), zoning and neighbor tolerance. We broker the lease, run pre-development diligence and later sell a 'depot-in-a-box' kit.
why_now: Waymo and others have announced 2026 expansion to many more metros using fleet partners, interconnection is the chokepoint, and office and parking distress is deep.
revenue_model: Broker fee of 4-6% of first-year rent, $5-10K per month site-package subscriptions from fleets, and landowner listing fees.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is electric service already in place, and 'obsolete' vacant buildings hold plenty. The best robotaxi real estate may be a half-empty garage with a multi-megawatt service, not airport-adjacent industrial land.
first_30_days: Compile 300 candidate sites in two launching metros. Call the local depot leads at fleet operators and deliver a 'power-ready shortlist' for $5K. Sign one or two exclusive landowner listings.

title: Fill the Empty EU Wallet: Payroll Attestations
one_liner: Issue consented, selectively disclosed employment-and-income attestations from payroll systems into EU Digital Identity Wallets, sold per verification to rental platforms, lenders and landlords fighting AI-forged payslips.
customer: Relying parties: rental and housing platforms, property managers and letting agents, consumer lenders, car-lease and telecom-contract sellers, paying EUR 0.50-3 per verified income or employment check. The issuing side is payroll providers and mid-size employers, who get a revenue share.
problem: Every member state must offer a wallet by 24 Dec 2026, and banks, telecoms and large platforms must accept it by late 2027. But a wallet holding only an ID card is a dud. The credentials people actually need to prove (income, employment, licences, tenancy history) sit in payroll and HR systems with no issuing channel. Meanwhile generative AI makes forged payslips and employment letters trivial, and landlords and lenders either eat fraud or manually call employers.
solution: An attestation issuance gateway that plugs into payroll platforms and APIs. After employee consent it issues short-lived, signed 'employment status and income band' attestations, using a qualified trust service provider partner for qualified status. Selective disclosure proves 'net income at least 3x rent' without revealing salary. A relying-party SDK and REST API handle verification. Start in rental applications in one market with acute fraud pain, such as the Netherlands, Germany or Spain. Before wallets go live, sell the same check as a QR-verifiable signed document.
why_now: The 24 Dec 2026 wallet deadline and late-2027 acceptance mandates create a supply gap. QEAA implementing rules exist. Generative forgery has collapsed trust in PDFs, and payroll vendors do not want to build issuance and carry the liability.
revenue_model: Per-verification fees of EUR 0.50-3 from relying parties, with 30% shared with the payroll provider. A white-label issuer licence for large payroll and HR vendors, and monthly minimums for landlord groups and lenders.
non_obvious_insight: Wallet adoption will be decided by which credentials are in it on day one, not by the wallet app. The two parties who want the wallet most, landlords and lenders, mainly need one credential (income) that lives in a system nobody has plugged in. Selective disclosure lets payroll data be monetized without exposing it, and the scarce asset is the issuer supply side.
first_30_days: Sign LOIs with two payroll providers (one small regional) and one rental platform or property manager group. Build a proof of concept against the EU reference wallet and a test QTSP. In parallel run a manual pre-wallet pilot where consenting employees get payroll-signed QR-verifiable income statements, so revenue starts before the wallet launches.

title: The 40 Days: Postpartum Confinement Caregiver Guild
one_liner: A trained, insured, tradition-certified caregiver guild delivering the 26 to 42 day postpartum confinement (yuesao, sanhujori, cuarentena) to diaspora families whose grandmothers are far away.
customer: New parents in Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, South Asian, Latino and Middle Eastern communities in dense metros, mostly mothers at 30 to 36 weeks. Secondary payers: extended-family gift funds and employers or health plans looking to reduce postpartum depression.
problem: Confinement care is widely practiced but supplied through informal agencies and word of mouth. A US yuesao runs about $200 to $400 a day for the standard 26 days, and a 42-day term adds roughly 60%. Quality, safety and worker protections vary widely, agencies rarely serve non-Chinese traditions, and parents without a grandmother nearby are left choosing between exhaustion and a gray-market caregiver.
solution: Build the guild rather than a marketplace. Recruit experienced caregivers and give them W-2 employment, insurance and background checks, plus training in safe sleep, lactation basics, infection control and postpartum warning signs with an escalation path to the family's OB or midwife. Certify them in specific traditions (menus, do's and don'ts) and match on language and tradition. Sell modular tiers: nights only, meals only, 14, 28 or 42 days. Add a plain-language guide for in-laws and partners.
why_now: Immigrant-heavy metros have a large unmet pool of families who want the ritual, and grandmothers are harder to bring over given tighter visa and travel rules. Employer-of-record and payroll tools make W-2 caregiver employment easy for a tiny company. Postpartum mental health is a rising priority for employers and health plans.
revenue_model: $5,500 to $12,000 per family per engagement, at about 30% to 35% gross margin after caregiver pay. Meals-only tier at $35 to $55 a day for faster revenue. Employer or plan subsidy of $1,000 to $2,000 per birth. A gift registry for extended family.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is the trusted caregiver, so the moat is a certified workforce (training, payroll, insurance, safety escalation), not a listing site. Confinement is also the same intervention American medicine now calls the fourth trimester, so obstetric practices can refer to it without endorsing folk claims, and it has been an informal cash market that has never been professionalized.
first_30_days: Pick one metro with a dense Chinese-American or Korean-American community such as the San Gabriel Valley, Flushing or the Bay Area. Recruit 8 experienced caregivers through WeChat groups and existing agencies. Write a three-day training and safety protocol with a postpartum nurse and lactation consultant. Sign 10 founding families with a service guarantee, and sell a meals-only tier to 50 families for faster revenue. Line up two OB practices or doulas for referrals, and set up employer-of-record payroll.

title: Assay-Verified Swarf Pooling for Machine Shops
one_liner: Turn the chip bin into a revenue line: two-bin alloy segregation, assayed weekly pickup, and pooled truckloads sold direct to mills and remelters.
customer: Ohio job shops and mid-size plants (20-300 employees) machining stainless, nickel alloys, titanium, brass or tool steel, especially aerospace, energy and medical suppliers. The first buyer is the plant manager or owner. A second buyer is any prime or OEM that wants a closed-loop 'revert' chain-of-custody.
problem: The chip bin is the only place in a shop where money leaves blind. Most shops tip all chips into one roll-off. The scrap yard grades by eye or its own XRF and pays a mixed-lot price. One shovel of aluminum in 316 stainless, or too much cutting oil, can drop the price by 30%-70%, while clean, segregated titanium and nickel-alloy turnings sell at multiples of mixed scrap. Nobody at the shop has time to sort, and small volumes are too tiny for mills to accept directly.
solution: 'SwarfStack': color-coded, RFID-tagged two- and three-bin systems in the shop, plus a weekly route truck with an onboard scale and a handheld XRF that assays each pickup and logs photo, weight, alloy and oil content to a shared ledger. A centrifuge or briquetter handles the oil. Pool by alloy across dozens of shops into full truckloads sold directly to mills, foundries and remelters. Pay the shop 70%-80% of net price and issue a digital scrap certificate for chain-of-custody. The provenance data becomes more valuable as metals tariffs increasingly reward proof of where metal was melted.
why_now: Reshoring is adding domestic machining hours, and with them chips. Metals lead times and alloy volatility keep prices high. The April 2026 Section 232 rewrite taxes the full customs value of metal derivatives and gives better treatment to U.S.-melted content, so provenance now has a price. Used handheld XRF analyzers now cost about what a used pickup does, and cheap vision models can identify alloy family from a photo of a bin.
revenue_model: A 20%-30% spread between the pooled sale price and what the shop is paid, plus $150-$300 per month bin and route fees, plus a small fee per digital scrap certificate. A route with 60 shops averaging $1,500 per month of chip value nets about $250k-$400k per year, before adding a briquetting and coolant-recovery arm.
non_obvious_insight: The scrap dealer's edge is not market power, it is that the shop does not know what is in its own bin. The metal was worth far more than the 'mixed' price, and shops give away five-figure sums each year without ever seeing the invoice line.
first_30_days: Buy a used handheld XRF for about $15k-$25k and rent a pickup with a platform scale. Sign 8 aerospace and medical suppliers in one county, starting with those cutting titanium, Inconel or stainless. Run pickups, assay each load, and send each shop a 'you left $X in your bin' statement showing the uplift against their current dealer. Pre-sell pooled loads to one stainless remelter and one titanium remelter before the first truckload.

title: Release-Date Congestion Map and Collision Cover
one_liner: A wishlist-overlap model and anonymous date-slot registry that tells indies where launch windows are crowded, later backed by parametric cover if a mega-title lands on top of them.
customer: Self-publishing indie developers and small publishers with 20k+ wishlists, and later insurers and MGAs underwriting launch risk.
problem: GTA VI launches 2026-11-19, and other publishers are rescheduling around it. Silksong (about 5.2M wishlists, 7M+ sales by Dec 2025) pushed several indies to delay after its date was announced. Devs lock marketing spend, then a giant date shifts. When everyone dodges the same date, they pile into the same safe windows, creating new collisions.
solution: Ingest public Steam wishlist ranks, release calendars and creator schedules to produce a congestion map and a per-title collision score based on audience overlap. Add a confidential slot registry where publishers submit intended dates and get congestion feedback. Once loss data exists, add parametric cover paying out if a listed mega-title moves within +/-14 days of a locked date.
why_now: GTA VI is the largest release-calendar shock in years and its ripple lasts months. Q1 2027 herd behavior is forming now, and no one measures collision risk.
revenue_model: $49-299 per month SaaS or $500 per date report, plus a 15-25% MGA commission on parametric premiums (3-6% of cover).
non_obvious_insight: Collision is treated as luck, but it is measurable through audience overlap and tradeable as a parametric risk. The herd effect, everyone avoiding the same date, is a coordination failure a neutral registry can fix.
first_30_days: Scrape Steam release calendars and wishlist ranks. Publish a free Q1 2027 congestion map on Discord and Reddit dev communities. Sell 20 paid date reports and speak to 3 MGAs about a pilot cover.

title: Reef Mixtapes for Oyster Hatcheries and Reefs
one_liner: Underwater speakers and a licensed library of healthy-reef soundscapes that lure oyster larvae to settle in hatchery tanks and restoration sites.
customer: Oyster hatcheries and remote-setting operations, oyster farmers, and restoration NGOs and state shellfish agencies such as those running large reef programs.
problem: Larval settlement is a costly bottleneck: eyed larvae are expensive to raise and many fail to set on cultch. Restoration reefs built on bare bottom get poor recruitment because they are silent, while healthy reefs act like acoustic beacons.
solution: A plug-in kit of a waterproof speaker, a controller and a subscription to species- and region-specific reef sound libraries recorded on healthy local reefs (snapping-shrimp crackle in the 1.5-20 kHz range). It ships with a built-in split-tank A/B protocol so any hatchery can measure the settlement gain in a week. Restoration clients can pay per acre on measured recruitment. Later products: playback buoys and acoustic tuning per species.
why_now: The science is now credible and publicised. Lab playbacks showed more oyster settlement under reef sound than under soft-bottom sound or silence (Lillis et al., PLOS ONE 2013), and later work reported large increases. In July 2026 WHOI, with The Nature Conservancy Massachusetts and shellfish constables, began a two-year effort to build a 'New England mixtape' for farmers and restorers. Rugged hydrophones and speakers are cheap. Nobody has yet packaged this for commerce.
revenue_model: Hardware kit at roughly $600-1,500, a library subscription of $50-150 per month per site, and performance-based restoration contracts (for example a share of measured settlement gains or per-acre fees). Longer term, license the sound and response dataset to acoustic-restoration players.
non_obvious_insight: Larvae navigate by ear, and degraded reefs are literally silent, so sound is a cheap cue you can sell. The defensible asset is the proprietary library of local recordings plus the settlement-response data by species and region. Commercial-hatchery effect sizes are still unproven, so the honest first product is the A/B testing rig and pay-on-results pricing, which turns scientific uncertainty into the sales pitch.
first_30_days: Buy two hydrophones and two speakers. Get three small hatcheries to run split-tank A/B settlement counts with a simple protocol, and record one healthy reef per region. Publish the first results and convert the hatcheries with the strongest lift into paying $1,500 kits.

title: Interim Smoke-Damage Protocol Before the State Standard
one_liner: Publish and run the defensible smoke, ash and soot assessment protocol that California insurers, adjusters and lawyers will need on January 1, 2027, because the official technical standard will not exist until 2028-2029.
customer: California carriers, the FAIR Plan and their TPAs (for AB 1795's 30-day inspection and testing obligations), plus public adjusters, policyholder attorneys, and escrow, lender and buyer parties in standing-home sales. Homeowners pay via their insurer, PA or directly.
problem: California signed AB 1795 and AB 1642 on Sept 15, 2026. From Jan 1, 2027, insurers must inspect within 30 days, pay for necessary testing, keep paying ALE until restoration, and face a presumption that ash, soot and char in a standing home are fire-caused. But the state toxics department will not finish lead and asbestos standards until end of 2028 and other contaminant standards until 2029. Meanwhile tens of thousands of claims will need a protocol that survives litigation; existing vendor assessments are already accused of being substandard, and capacity of qualified industrial hygienists is scarce and expensive.
solution: An independent, openly published interim assessment protocol built on existing standards (IICRC S700, established sampling and lab methods, EPA/HUD dust-wipe criteria), developed with certified industrial hygienists and a toxicologist. Delivered as a product: a sampling-plan generator (which rooms, surfaces and ducts, how many samples), a trained technician network with kits and a chain-of-custody app, remote IH sign-off, a lab partner, a compliance-clock dashboard for carriers, and a 'smoke clearance certificate' for resale and escrow. Priced at a fraction of full CIH scopes.
why_now: The laws were signed two weeks ago with an effective date of Jan 1, 2027, LA County is investigating Farmers over Eaton/Palisades claim denials, a proposed class action targets vendor assessments, and carriers oppose but must comply. The gap between the compliance date and the state standard is a 2-3 year window in which the best-documented protocol becomes the de facto reference, and other fire states (Colorado, Oregon, Hawaii) are watching.
revenue_model: Per-home assessment of $1,800-$4,500 (paid by insurer under AB 1795 or the policyholder), $500 clearance-certificate add-on, lab pass-through margin, SaaS compliance dashboard for carriers at $2-$5 per claim per month, and training and certification fees for restoration technicians.
non_obvious_insight: In smoke disputes the lab is rarely the fight; the fight is the sampling design and the pass/fail threshold. Carriers whose vendors sample five spots and compare against urban background dust get 'clean' results by construction. Whoever publishes a transparent, replicable sampling grid with chain of custody writes the eventual standard, because regulators borrow the protocol with the most field data.
first_30_days: Recruit two CIHs and one toxicologist as an advisory board and draft 'Interim Smoke Assessment Protocol v0.1' for public comment. Train 6-10 IICRC-certified restoration technicians and buy sampling kits. Sell 20 pilot assessments in Altadena and Palisades at a subsidized $950 through public adjusters and attorneys, gathering data and case studies. Pitch 3 carriers and 2 TPAs on 30-day compliance capacity before January 1, offering a pilot at cost in exchange for using the protocol.

title: Live-Action Fraud Drills Using Immersive Theater
one_liner: Ticketed and B2B immersive-theater experiences where participants, with consent, get scammed by actors and voice-cloned 'relatives' in a safe space and learn the tells under real emotional pressure.
customer: Credit unions, community banks and insurers that want measurable fraud-loss reduction among older customers; employers' security teams and finance, HR and IT-helpdesk staff (named targets of voice deepfakes); senior-living operators, libraries and AARP-style chapters. Escape-room and immersive-theater operators are licensees.
problem: Per the briefing, adults 60+ lost $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), account for 66% of crypto-ATM losses, and law-enforcement-impersonation scams produced about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B+ with fake video calls. Conventional awareness training (videos, phishing simulations) shows little measurable effect; a 2025 study of about 19,500 UCSD Health employees found annual training had almost no impact on click rates (verify). Voice cloning now needs only 3 seconds of audio. The pressure tactics (urgency, secrecy, authority) are exactly what a lecture cannot simulate.
solution: A repeatable, franchisable 60-90 minute experience. Participants get a 'phone call' from an actor-controlled voice clone of a consenting volunteer (real-time voice conversion trained on the volunteer's own sample) or a fake CFO. They move through an escalating fraud script (fake bank, 'police', crypto-ATM instructions) with hidden facilitators, then a debrief teaches three tells and sets up a family or team safe-word protocol. Each participant leaves with a personalised safe-word card and help turning on their bank's trusted-contact feature. A B2B mobile 30-minute 'CFO voice-clone drill' scores the sponsor on how many people stop the transfer at each step. Outcomes are measured pre/post and at 90 days. Psychological-safety protocol and a counselor are built in.
why_now: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, when awareness budgets are spent. The FBI's 17 Sep 2026 PSA cites AI video calls in law-enforcement impersonation. Real-time voice conversion is cheap and voice-deepfake attacks are surging. Regulators are pushing banks to protect vulnerable customers (for example the UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement since Oct 2024), so banks want provable prevention.
revenue_model: Sponsors pay $3-8k per community event of 30-60 participants, or $40-150 per employee for corporate drills. Licensing or franchise fees from venues (about $1.5k/month plus event share). Public ticketed shows at $25-40 with sponsor underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud victims are not ignorant. They are overwhelmed by staged emotion under time pressure, and skills learned in calm classrooms fail under stress. Live-experience designers know how to induce and safely release exactly that state, and security teams know the real scripts. Banks can also compute ROI in avoided losses, which theater companies cannot.
first_30_days: Pair an immersive-theater company with a fraud investigator. Prototype a 45-minute 'grandparent scam' and a 'CFO deepfake' scenario with consent forms and a licensed counselor. Pilot with two credit unions and one library during October at about $2.5k each. Measure pre/post behavior with a follow-up test call. Use results to sell to regional credit-union leagues and security-awareness teams.

title: Compute-Heated Housing: GPUs as the Boiler Room
one_liner: Put a liquid-cooled AI rack in an apartment tower's mechanical room and use its waste heat as the building's hot-water plant, cutting utility costs while hosting power-starved compute.
customer: Owners of 200-500 unit towers or planned conversions with central hot-water plants, especially in cities with building-emissions caps, paired with inference and neocloud operators seeking power and cooling.
problem: 20.7% of renters cannot pay utilities in full, gas boilers face per-ton fines under building-performance laws (NYC Local Law 97 tightens in 2030), and AI compute is starved for sites with power and cooling.
solution: Install one direct-liquid-cooled rack (about 100-130 kW) in the mechanical room. Capture waste heat, lift it with heat pumps to domestic hot water, and sell the building heat at a discount to gas or provide it free in exchange for hosting. The compute operator pays colocation rent, and we own design, integration and the thermal contract. Later expand to space heating and whole conversions.
why_now: Dense liquid-cooled racks produce capturable heat, AI power scarcity is acute, heat-pump hot water is mature, and building-emissions caps are tightening.
revenue_model: Heat-as-a-service at 30-40% of avoided energy cost, hosting margin share, and $25-50K design fees per building.
non_obvious_insight: By rough engineering estimate, a 300-unit building's average hot-water load (about 100-120 kW thermal) roughly equals one AI rack's heat output. The boiler room can host compute that cannot be sited elsewhere, and hot-water demand never sleeps. Precedents exist in Europe (data-furnace heaters and pool heating).
first_30_days: Run feasibility on five NYC and Chicago buildings with emissions-cap exposure. Get a letter of intent from one inference host for a 100 kW pilot. Sell three paid feasibility studies at $10-15K and line up host-funded pilot capex.

title: CPAP Off-Ramp: Retire Machines, Refurbish for Uninsured
one_liner: Re-test sleep apnea at each weight-loss milestone, help patients who have gone into remission safely come off CPAP, and refurbish the retired machines for the newly uninsured.
customer: Medicare Advantage plans and self-insured employers (paying a share of avoided rental and supply costs), cash-pay GLP-1 patients paying for the recheck, and safety-net clinics buying refurbished units.
problem: Tirzepatide is approved for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity, and in SURMOUNT-OSA 43% to 52% of patients at the top dose met disease-resolution criteria, with apnea-hypopnea events cut by up to about 60%. Nobody is paid to notice. DME suppliers earn on continued mask and hose resupply, sleep labs earn on tests, and patients keep machines in the closet. After 13 months of Medicare rental the patient owns the machine, so it can simply be donated. Meanwhile about 4.8M people are newly uninsured after the ACA subsidy expiry, with millions more Medicaid losses due in 2027, and a $800-1,000 CPAP is out of reach.
solution: A physician-supervised pathway with a disposable home sleep apnea test at each 10% weight-loss milestone and a telehealth sleep-physician review. Patients who qualify taper or stop PAP, and are offered a buy-back credit or donation. Returned machines are sanitized, function-tested, data-wiped and re-kitted with new humidifier chambers, filters and tubing, then re-issued via licensed DME partners and clinics at roughly $150-250. Motors, foam and plastics from units that fail go to recycling.
why_now: Zepbound's OSA indication is now established and Part D can cover it. The cash-pay pill wave and the July 2026 Medicare Bridge bring far more patients on-drug. ACA and Medicaid losses create a cash-pay buyer base for cheap devices.
revenue_model: Performance fee from payers or employers of about 30% of first-year avoided rental and supply cost. Cash-pay recheck ($79-129). Margin on refurbished device sales, with a nonprofit partner able to receive donation tax deductions.
non_obvious_insight: GLP-1 success silently strands both a recurring billing stream and a physical asset. The party that finds the stranded machine can be paid twice: once by the payer for the avoided spend and once by the uninsured buyer for the second life.
first_30_days: Contract a tele-sleep physician group and a licensed DME partner. Recruit 100 patients from a cash-pay telehealth partner who have OSA and are on tirzepatide. Write the refurbishment SOP against manufacturer cleaning guidance and state DME rules. Sell the first payer or employer pilot on a savings-share basis with retrospective claims data.

title: Overtourism Feed for AI Travel Agents
one_liner: A destination-signed, machine-readable feed of live capacity, closures and dispersal incentives that AI trip agents query, so places can steer planning before tourists arrive.
customer: Destination management organisations and city tourism boards in overtouristed regions (Balearics, Dolomites, Kyoto, Lisbon, Dubrovnik, Amsterdam), later transport agencies and hotel groups.
problem: AI agents now plan and book trips (Booking.com and Expedia apps run inside ChatGPT), and they recommend the same hotspots blind to caps, closures and crowding. DMOs intervene only after arrival with fees and fines, which Venice's reportedly ineffective day-tripper fee shows is weak. Referral traffic from search is being eaten by AI answers.
solution: Publish an MCP server and JSON feed per destination with a daily load index by place and hour (from ticketing, parking, cruise calendars and occupancy), hard caps and permits, equivalent alternatives within about 60 minutes with partner lodging, resident-first hours and off-peak incentive codes. DMOs get a dashboard showing how many agent-planned trips shifted. Start with a hosted API and a DMO-embedded chatbot for immediate use.
why_now: OTA apps are now inside AI assistants, MCP servers are mainstream, booking lead times are shrinking, and AI overviews reportedly cut metasearch clicks by 31% in tested markets. DMOs need a way to influence the plan rather than the queue.
revenue_model: DMO subscriptions of EUR 20-100K per year, transparent sponsored 'dispersal' placements paid by under-visited partners, and analytics.
non_obvious_insight: Overtourism control is an information-timing problem. Influence must happen at itinerary generation, and AI agents are the first chokepoint where a single feed can shape millions of itineraries, giving destinations robots.txt-style power.
first_30_days: Build a feed for one region from public data (cruise schedules, park permit status, museum time slots) and ship the MCP server. Offer 3 DMOs a free traffic dashboard as design partners and embed it in their own website chatbots. Approach trip-planner app builders for consumption.

title: Landing Fund: Sweden's Layoff Council for US Employers
one_liner: Employers pay about 0.3% of payroll into a pooled transition fund that gives every laid-off employee case management, retraining money and bridge pay, so companies can restructure without severance drama.
customer: CFOs and CHROs at 200-3,000-employee US companies (software, fintech, insurance, BPO, media) that are restructuring around AI or expect to. Reached through PEOs, HR brokers and benefits consultants.
problem: US severance is ad hoc (about 12-14 weeks for white-collar staff) and outplacement is usually a webinar. Leaders delay or botch layoffs because there is no humane, pre-agreed answer to 'what happens to the people we cut.' One tracker counts roughly 205,000 AI-attributed US layoffs through August 2026, concentrated in entry-level and back-office roles.
solution: A US version of Sweden's Trygghetsrådet (TRR). Employers join a pool at a set percentage of payroll. When someone is laid off they get a named case manager, retraining vouchers, a 2-4 month bridge-pay top-up, and a COBRA/health bridge subsidy, with providers paid partly on outcomes. Employers get a standard offboarding playbook, smaller bespoke severance, and less litigation and survivor-morale damage. Launch as prepaid 'transition credits' (no insurance license needed) and graduate to a captive or reinsured product.
why_now: AI became the top stated reason for corporate job cuts in the spring of 2026, entry-level white-collar hiring has collapsed, and executives are being publicly punished for how they lay people off. In Sweden the model covers 30,000+ companies and about 700,000 employees on 0.3% of payroll, and roughly 9 in 10 active clients found work, study or self-employment within seven months (2019 figures).
revenue_model: Per-employee-per-month or a percentage of payroll (0.2-0.4%). Unspent reserves fund the next cohort, with margin on training-partner rev share and, later, insurance float.
non_obvious_insight: Sweden's system works because employers fund it collectively, so no single firm carries the full cost of a big layoff, and that pooling turns a dreaded cost into a predictable premium. The buyer's real pain is decision speed and reputation, not the money. A ready-made, respected answer to 'what about the people' lets an executive act faster and more humanely, which is why the product can sell before any regulator asks for it.
first_30_days: Build a 'layoff readiness pack' (offboarding checklist, manager scripts, fund terms) and pitch 15 mid-size companies through two PEOs and an HR consultancy. Line up two training providers and one career-coaching group. Target letters of intent from 5-10 founding employers covering about 5,000 employees at roughly $15 per employee per month, with a first paying pool by month 3.

title: Skin-Tone-Verified SpO2 Validation Cooperative
one_liner: Build the 10x-larger, objectively skin-tone-measured, arterial-blood-paired dataset that pulse-oximeter and wearable makers need, and sell access, bias reports and validation studies.
customer: Pulse-oximeter and wearable OEMs and startups, plus hospital purchasing groups that want independent bias reports before buying devices.
problem: Current pulse oximeters tend to overestimate arterial saturation in darkly pigmented patients, so low oxygen can go undetected. A new arXiv correction method works on 98 patients from the public OpenOximetry Repository but the authors say a cohort roughly ten times larger is needed for significance. The 2013 FDA 510(k) guidance asks for only 'at least 2 darkly pigmented subjects or 15% of your subject pool' and says nothing of objective pigmentation measures.
solution: Recruit a diverse cohort and characterize each participant with a skin reflectance spectrometer to get melanin fraction. Run induced-hypoxia studies with paired arterial samples through partner university hypoxia labs. License the de-identified dataset and calibration models to OEMs, and offer per-device bias validation and a public 'bias report card' for hospital buyers.
why_now: The 2026 arXiv paper by Blaney, Fantini, Koomson and colleagues shows a melanin-aware correction that cut error from +2.8 to +0.1 percentage points per unit melanin fraction, but it is data-limited. Wearable SpO2 features are now mainstream, and regulators and buyers are asking for skin-tone-diverse evidence. I could not verify in this session the status of the January 2025 FDA draft guidance, so confirm it before pitching.
revenue_model: Dataset licenses of roughly $50-250k, per-device validation studies of $100-400k, and annual bias-report subscriptions for hospital groups and OEMs.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is data, not algorithms. The arXiv paper says current oximeters 'overestimate arterial saturation in darkly pigmented patients', its correction relies on per-patient skin-tone measurement, and 'a cohort roughly ten times larger is needed' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30122). The current FDA 510(k) guidance sets a low bar of 2 darkly pigmented subjects or 15% of the pool (https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/pulse-oximeters-premarket-notification-submissions-510ks-guidance-industry-and-food-and-drug). Whoever owns the largest objectively measured dataset sets the de facto standard, and every OEM has to buy or replicate it.
first_30_days: Email the arXiv authors and OpenOximetry contributors about their data needs. Sign a partner hypoxia lab and an IRB pathway, and design a 30-50 participant pilot. Pre-sell the pilot dataset to 3 wearable or oximeter startups through LOIs. Prototype a spectrometer-based melanin measurement protocol and publish a pre-registered study plan.

title: Compliance Co-op for Group-Buy Hobby Hardware
one_liner: A pooled EU compliance desk (CRA incident reporting, EU responsible person, battery/e-waste registrations, SBOM monitoring) that lets one-person keyboard, FPV, synth and LoRa hardware makers keep selling to Europe.
customer: Boutique hardware makers of 1-20 people in enthusiast scenes: custom mechanical keyboards, eurorack/synth modules, FPV drone boards, LoRa/Meshtastic radios, 3D-printer upgrade kits. They sell through group buys, Tindie, Kickstarter and Discord shops, including US and Asian makers shipping into the EU/UK, plus the boutique vendors that resell them.
problem: Per the briefing, the EU Cyber Resilience Act's 24-hour vulnerability/incident reporting duty went live 11 Sep 2026 for products with digital elements, Data Act connected-product design duties began 12 Sep 2026, and full CRA conformity is due 11 Dec 2027 (fines up to EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover). Those duties fall on whoever sells the product, and in hobby scenes that is a hobbyist selling a 300-unit run built on open-source firmware (QMK, Betaflight, Klipper, Meshtastic). The CRA's open-source carve-out protects non-commercial projects, not the person selling hardware with the firmware. Stack on the EU General Product Safety Regulation's EU-responsible-person requirement (in force since Dec 2024), radio-equipment cybersecurity rules, and battery and WEEE registrations (battery labelling duties start around Aug 2026, verify), and the makers' choices are to ignore it or stop shipping to the EU. A EUR 5-10k consultancy engagement is impossible on an $80-300 product.
solution: A membership 'compliance-of-record' co-op. Members get: a named EU responsible person and CRA contact of record (professional-indemnity insured); a shared coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure desk with a tested runbook for filing on ENISA's single reporting platform within 24 hours; a CI plug-in that generates SBOMs and watches firmware dependencies (QMK, ChibiOS, ESP-IDF, Zephyr etc.) for exploited CVEs; declaration-of-conformity and technical-file templates by product class; a battery/EPR registration bundle; and a group-buy contract addendum covering delivery windows and customised-goods withdrawal rights. The co-op also acts as liaison to upstream open-source firmware projects and channels 'sponsored security fixes' to them.
why_now: CRA reporting has been live for about 18 days and the Data Act design duties for 17 (per briefing). Market-surveillance sweeps and marketplace delistings typically follow such dates, and marketplaces already delist listings that lack GPSR data. Full conformity lands 11 Dec 2027, so scenes will look for a shared answer during 2026-27, before any vendor has locked the niche.
revenue_model: Annual dues tiered by EU units shipped (about EUR 390/yr up to 500 units, EUR 1,200 up to 5,000, custom above). Per-SKU onboarding fee of EUR 250-750. Optional micro-levy of EUR 0.10-0.25 per unit that funds the incident desk and upstream firmware maintainers. Paid 'CRA sprint' for makers with more than 5 SKUs.
non_obvious_insight: Regulators wrote these rules for companies with a compliance department, but the enthusiast hardware economy is thousands of micro-manufacturers who share the same three failure points: firmware dependencies, 24-hour incident reporting, and an EU address. The scalable unit of compliance is the scene or firmware ecosystem, not the individual maker. A co-op that pools the boring 80% and is trusted inside the scene's Discords beats both a law firm and a generic authorised-representative vendor, because reputation in the scene is the distribution channel.
first_30_days: Pick one scene (custom keyboards on QMK/VIA, or LoRa/Meshtastic). Interview 15 makers from group-buy vendor lists. Have a compliance lawyer and a firmware engineer write a one-page '24-hour CRA reporting runbook' and post it free in the scene's Discords, r/MechanicalKeyboards and Geekhack. Sign 10 founding members at about EUR 250 for year one, deliver an incident-reporting drill and a template technical file for one product class, and sell fixed-price single-SKU audits. Cost is two part-time experts plus a simple site, and break-even is roughly 40 members.

title: Exosuit-as-a-Service Paid by Workers' Comp Carriers
one_liner: Rentable powered back-and-hip assist suits for home-care aides and nursing assistants, with usage data that earns workers' comp premium credits.
customer: Home-care agencies and nursing-home operators with high workers' comp experience mods, workers' comp carriers and MGAs with loss-control budgets, and PEOs.
problem: Aides and nursing assistants have some of the highest musculoskeletal injury rates, and a claim costs tens of thousands. Agencies can't install ceiling lifts in clients' homes, and with 77-80% turnover, injuries drive both cost and churn.
solution: Rent-by-month lightweight powered assist suits with sizing, training and warranty. Onboard sensors count bends and lifts to build injury-risk analytics for the carrier, who credits premiums. Start with clients who need transfers, and use it as a retention perk.
why_now: Consumer-priced powered exosuits appeared in 2025-26, and workforce scarcity makes worker safety and retention perks valuable. Comp carriers are actively looking for loss-control programs in a squeezed home-health margin environment.
revenue_model: $60-100 per suit per month paid by the agency or shared with the carrier, performance rebates, and an analytics subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Sell to the party that pays for injuries (the carrier), not the aide, and let data turn a gadget into a premium negotiation. Lab claims of strain reduction still need real-world proof, which the pilot supplies.
first_30_days: Lease 30 suits from an OEM, find two agencies and a regional comp carrier, and run a 90-day trial measuring injuries, lost workdays and turnover.

title: Displaced Insurance Agents Become Rooftop Solar Navigators
one_liner: Recruit the micro-agents wiped out by India's proposed insurance commission cuts as the trust-and-paperwork channel for rooftop solar, batteries and induction retrofits, paid per install by installers and lenders.
customer: MNRE-empanelled EPC installers and lenders (PSU banks, NBFCs) who pay per verified install or disbursed loan. The micro-agents (POSPs, motor-insurance agents, CSC operators) are the supply side.
problem: IRDAI's 2026-09-23 draft cuts general-insurance commission caps from 30% to 20%, sets 0% on motor third-party and 5% on own-damage, and PB Fintech fell 36% in one day. Hundreds of thousands of small agents in tier-2 and tier-3 towns lose most of their income. Meanwhile household solar and electrification demand is throttled by last-mile trust and paperwork (DISCOM feasibility, net-metering, subsidy claims, loans) rather than by hardware cost.
solution: A navigator app with training and payout rails. The agent walks a household through eligibility, vendor selection, DISCOM application, subsidy claim, bank loan and insurance for the new asset, earning per completed milestone. The annual motor-renewal touchpoint becomes the sales moment, and battery and induction bundles are added. The platform handles KYC, lead routing, quality control and payouts.
why_now: The IRDAI draft is days old and distributors such as PolicyBazaar and Turtlemint are squeezed and looking for new products. India's government-backed rooftop programs (verify current PM Surya Ghar terms) and LPG-shock induction demand are pulling households toward electrification, and UPI makes micro-payouts cheap.
revenue_model: INR 3,000-6,000 per installed home from the EPC (about 2-4% of net system cost), INR 1,000-2,000 per loan from lenders, insurance attach for the new asset, with the platform keeping 20-30% of bounties.
non_obvious_insight: Regulation just stranded a trusted, KYC'd, paperwork-fluent field force at the exact moment the bottleneck in electrification moved from hardware cost to last-mile trust. Insurance micro-agents are a distribution network searching for a product, and rooftop solar is a product searching for distribution.
first_30_days: Recruit 50 agents in one district through motor-insurance agent WhatsApp and Telegram communities and CSC networks. Sign 2 local EPCs on a per-commissioned-install bounty, run 20 installs end to end, and measure conversion from renewal touchpoints. Pay agents by UPI after commissioning.

title: Succession Roll-Up for Retiring Solo Therapists
one_liner: A service that brokers and buys retiring solo practices and transitions clients to vetted associates, so clients are not orphaned and young clinicians inherit a full caseload.
customer: Retiring psychologists, social workers and family therapists (paid through fees and earn-outs) and early-career clinicians or group practices paying a transition fee, roughly $3-10k per practice.
problem: A large share of independent therapists are past 55, and solo practitioners typically just close, leaving clients scrambling. New clinicians spend 12-24 months building a caseload. Consolidation is capturing platform-dependent supply (Spring Health acquiring Alma, Jan 2026; Universal Health Services buying Talkspace for $835M, Mar 2026), but nobody owns practice transition the way dental service organizations do.
solution: A 6-12 month warm-handoff program consistent with ethics codes and client choice: records custody, client consent workflow, payer-panel reassignment through a group NPI, referral-source handover, and an earn-out to the retiring clinician funded by the successor's collections. Software handles consent, records and payer onboarding. Later: an MSO owning the transitioned practices.
why_now: Back-office rails built by Alma and Grow (Grow raised $150M) now make onboarding an associate cheap. Boomer therapists retire through 2025-30, and platform consolidation leaves the independent tail unowned.
revenue_model: Transition fee (5-10% of annual practice revenue), earn-out spread, later MSO margin, and buyer-side subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is consolidating the platform, but nobody is consolidating the goodwill of retiring clinicians, which is the cheapest source of established caseloads and referral relationships and the one asset that walks out the door every Friday.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 retiring clinicians through state association mailings and Psychology Today profiles. Match five with early-career clinicians. Have a healthcare attorney draft an ethics-reviewed transition agreement, and complete two transitions at a flat $3k each.

title: Off-the-Record Governance for AI Meeting Transcripts
one_liner: A policy layer over Zoom, Teams and Meet notetakers that decides what becomes 'the record'. It auto-pauses for privileged talk, purges verbatim transcripts once counsel-approved minutes are certified, and blocks unauthorized bots.
customer: General counsel and compliance leads at regulated mid-market companies with 200-5,000 employees, such as healthcare systems, fintechs, biotechs and defense contractors. Also law firms and corporate secretaries who run board minutes.
problem: AI notetakers made every meeting a verbatim, discoverable and error-prone transcript by default. A wrong attribution, such as 'we knew' instead of 'we know,' can become an exhibit. Third-party bots joining privileged calls raise waiver risk. Recording-consent class actions against AI notetaker vendors are rising, especially in all-party-consent states. General counsel have no control primitive between 'record everything' and 'ban notetakers.'
solution: A meeting-level record mode with three states: on the record, off the record and privileged. It is enforced through calendar tags, participant signals (a lawyer joins, so transcript is suppressed) and admin APIs for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. Verbatim transcripts carry retention timers (7-30 days, unless a legal hold applies). A named human designee approves a summary, which becomes the sole record with an attestation stamp modeled on a reporter's certificate. Add an audit log and a bot allow-list. It sits on top of the notetakers the company already uses.
why_now: Enterprises spent 2025-26 rolling out Copilot, Gemini and Zoom AI notes company-wide. Lawsuits over AI notetaker recording consent were filed in 2025. Regulators have punished off-channel record-keeping failures, so record governance is now a board-level topic. Legal teams are asking for controls now.
revenue_model: $6-$12 per user per month with a $25,000 annual minimum. An entry 'Record Risk Audit' as a fixed $5,000-$10,000 project that converts to the platform. A channel through employment and litigation law firms that advise clients on AI policy.
non_obvious_insight: Reporters live by one ritual, 'off the record,' a physical control (they stop writing) that AI notetakers lack. They also know that outside a proceeding a verbatim transcript is a liability, not an asset. Most companies are only now realizing they built a huge discoverable archive of casual speech.
first_30_days: Sell the $5,000 audit to 10 general counsel through ACC chapters and LinkedIn. Inventory each company's bot footprint from admin logs and deliver a policy template. Build a thin MVP using Microsoft Graph and Google admin APIs that flips transcription per meeting from calendar tags. Convert 3 audits into paid pilots.

title: Retreat Options for Eroding Oceanfront Homes
one_liner: An annual retainer that reserves a house-mover and demolition slot and triggers automatically when satellite-measured setback hits a preset distance.
customer: Owners of oceanfront and bluff homes on the Outer Banks and Cape Hatteras, Great Lakes bluffs, Maine and Nantucket, and California bluffs. Secondary buyers are lenders, county governments and the National Park Service.
problem: 32 oceanfront houses have collapsed along Cape Hatteras National Seashore since 2020, four in one February 2026 weekend. Owners bear removal costs of roughly $120K to demolish or $100K-$200K to move. NFIP pays nothing pre-collapse, and contractor capacity is overwhelmed exactly when it is needed. NFIP pre-collapse coverage has been proposed but not enacted.
solution: Pooled owners pay a retainer for two things. First, monthly satellite measurement of foundation-to-scarp or vegetation-line distance from 30-50 cm imagery, with pre-storm tasking, and archive imagery to compute each home's 5-10 year retreat rate. Second, pre-negotiated capacity with movers and demolition contractors. Preset thresholds automatically mobilise the contractor and deliver a dated evidence file. That file doubles as claim documentation if NFIP pre-collapse legislation passes and gives lenders and counties a trusted trigger. Structured as a service and capacity contract rather than insurance.
why_now: FEMA's lack of any pre-collapse option is national news in September 2026 (NPR), and the Outer Banks lost 20 Buxton houses in a year. Pre-collapse coverage legislation is pending. Cheap oversupplied commercial imagery makes pooled tasking affordable (one 25 km2 pass covers about 10 km of coast and hundreds of homes).
revenue_model: $1,800/yr retainer per home. An 8-10% referral fee on move or demolition jobs. County and NPS triage contracts. Lender monitoring feeds at $10-20 per loan per month.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is neither money nor measurement but contractor capacity at the moment of crisis. An option on that capacity, triggered by a measurement all parties trust, is a new kind of asset. Neighbours pooling their tasking makes the satellite cost trivial per home.
first_30_days: Sign 2 Outer Banks or Great Lakes house-movers and demolition firms to retainer terms. Pull archive imagery to compute 5-year retreat rates for about 200 threatened homes, then approach owner associations in Buxton and Rodanthe with each home's own curve. Enrol 10 homes at $1,200 founder pricing.

title: After-Hours Shop-Lab Leasing in Shrinking Schools
one_liner: A booking and insurance layer that rents idle high-school shops, labs and classrooms to apprenticeship programs, trade schools and microschools on nights and weekends.
customer: Declining-enrollment districts (facilities and business managers) and tenants: apprenticeship sponsors (JATCs, IEC and ABC chapters), Workforce Pell training providers, microschool operators.
problem: Chicago has 135k empty seats and more than 1,000 schools closed nationally in 2025-26. Districts are structurally slow to repurpose buildings and closures are politically toxic. Meanwhile trade programs need labs with power, ventilation and benches, and building their own costs millions.
solution: Inventory idle CTE shops, labs and gyms by the hour (power, ventilation, accessibility, parking), a standard license agreement with liability insurance and custodial and security add-ons, calendar and billing, and matching to tenants. Rent hours, not buildings, to avoid closure politics.
why_now: The enrollment cliff is squeezing budgets. Workforce Pell allows 49% of instruction to be outsourced for apprenticeship-linked programs, and data-center-driven electrician demand is growing training capacity needs.
revenue_model: 15-25% take of lab and classroom rent (typically $40-120 per hour) plus insurance and custodial add-on margin; optional district SaaS.
non_obvious_insight: The politically feasible move is not closing or selling but renting the hours between 4pm and 9pm. The tenants are already funded, and the district only has to approve a license, not a school closure.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 districts each with an underused shop or lab. Sign one apprenticeship sponsor as anchor tenant. Draft the standard license and insurance rider. List the first 10 rooms and measure rent per hour.
